description: We are a team of mechanical engineers and physics enthusiasts, seeking for new experiences. We want to create a project accessible to all ages in which we introduce astrophysics.
summary: While children are deeply fascinated by space, space exploration remains largely absent from elementary and middle school curricula. To bridge this gap, we created a collaborative, role-based educational game built in Scratch—a programming tool students already use in their Computer Science classes—that transforms the classroom into an interactive mission control center. Working together in distinct roles, students design, manage, and simulate a complete space mission across five core phases: building modular spacecraft by balancing weight and aerodynamics, navigating past space hazards, managing crew resources and ship repairs, executing precision landings under varying gravities, and operating rovers to collect and analyze planetary samples. By leveraging familiar school software, our solution requires zero additional infrastructure and brings hands-on STEM engineering, teamwork, and space discovery directly into the classroom.
details: Our project is an interactive, role-based educational game where elementary school students design, manage, and simulate a complete space mission. It is built using Scratch (a programming platform students already use in Computer Science classes), the classroom transforms into a mission control center. Students divide into specific roles (such as spacecraft design, navigation, and resource management) and collaborate to design, build and navigate a spacecraft, manage resources and analyze collected data. It fills the educational gap where space exploration is typically absent from elementary school, turns abstract engineering concepts into tangible, hands-on experiments, fosters collaboration and communication and makes NASA's open data accessible to primary school students. The intended impact of the project is to transform how young students experience space science—shifting it from a distant, purely theoretical subject into an exciting, participatory reality as well as ignite children's natural fascination with the universe, inspire the next generation of scientists and engineers, and make space education accessible in every classroom. Our project introduces a novel educational approach by gamifying real aerospace engineering dilemmas (like balancing mass, fuel, and safety trade-offs) into a collaborative multiplayer experience for kids. Our team considered a variety of factors such as engineering trade-offs, pedagogical age-appropriateness (translating complex aerospace concepts into simplified, engaging mechanics that elementary school students can easily grasp), technical feasibility (designing the game within Scratch to ensure it is smooth, reliable, and compatible with existing school computer labs) and user engagement and balance (ensuring teamwork is mandatory and that time and resources are balanced so players must think critically about every choice they make).
